ms.report:
Response to Reviewer Comment for Clarification re Compliance Documents
Dear Reviewers, 
There is one evidence requirement around the submission records of the compliance documents. Under the EUDR we are required to show that the farmers are who they say they are and that they are allowed to harvest. The best way to do this normally is actually to upload land tenure documents issued by the government, but what we found with the on-ground reality is that in the Local Government Area of Boki and the broader Cross River State, the government has not done the necessary mapping activities to do this. We are actually the first people doing land-use recording for these farmers. We are in touch with the local regulators on making sure once they do the surveying that the records are matched. 
We did however, ensure that during the onboarding process of a farmer, they were required to provide national ID records - this information was captured as part of the KYC / Compliance process. 
The evidence is in the Public Reports created -https://zengate-global.metabaseapp.com/public/dashboard/2c0efd28-9e78-4cee-b35a-1ecb9f5898bf?agent_id=&date=&field_size=&organisation_id=&tab=71-farmers. There is a pie-chart visual called "Compliance Documents Upload Status for Farmers" which shows how many of the farmers we onboarded provided their ID and had it verified in real-time by the onboarding agents. This is captured in the system as an entry alongside every farmer profile creation (e.g the national ID information is a similar data capture point as is their gender, name, date of birth, etc...) - the only difference is that it comes with an image uploaded into the system of them and their ID to prove it is them. 
I hope this clarification makes sense. 
﻿

A. Output: Full Cocoa Supply-Chain Traceability Implementation (Palmyra Pro)
A1. Output: End-to-End Cocoa Traceability System
Note for reviewers:
Quality Assurance (QA) is implemented as an embedded component across core workflows rather than as a standalone module.
・At sourcing: moisture content is recorded at intake
・At processing: moisture reduction is tracked during transformation
・At batch level: final moisture validation is performed during aggregation

This reflects real operational practices where QA checks occur at key control points across the supply chain.
Acceptance criteria:
・Recording of harvest events linked to mapped farms in the system
・Processing and batch management records with immutable on-chain linkage
・End-to-end audit trail visible on dashboard (access shared and anonymised for the Project Catalyst team)

A2. Output: Cardano RWA Oracle Integration (Merkle Oracle)
Note:
The oracle implementation leverages zenGate’s Merkle Trie-based Oracle design to support multi-data point capture required for real-world asset (RWA) use cases. This enables structured financial and sourcing data (e.g. cash payments linked to cocoa batches) to be grouped, hashed, and anchored on-chain efficiently, which is not supported by standard single-data-point oracle designs.
